brief: Oil supply fears (Saudi Yanbu terminal loadings suspended, Libyan output halted, no sign the Strait of Hormuz reopens) pushed Brent +2.90% to $108.75/bbl and WTI +4.38% to $105.83/bbl, reviving stagflation concern. That drove Treasury yields to multi-year highs: the 10yr closed above 5% for the first time since 2007, with real yields, 30yr and a weak 20yr auction all confirming the move; European yields hit similar post-2007/2008/2009 highs even as ECB October hike odds fell. Equities and Bitcoin sold off (S&P 6-week low, STOXX 3-month low, Bitcoin's worst day in three months after a Senate crypto bill failed) though both indices stayed within single digits of their highs. Separately, the note traces Fed hike odds from ~30% priced at the July hold, through Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks, to 94% priced for a hike today, the first since 2023, reinforced by a strong August jobs report and a hot core CPI print. DB's own economists expect the hike, and frame the key question as guidance: no explicit forward guidance, but a median dot showing one more 2026 hike, some officials projecting more.
